answer: Inference benchmarking curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to evaluate continuous neural tasks. Nodes classify randomized umber image tensors under tight deadlines, so attackers cannot let response latencies wander across shared hardware. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of dedicating GPU compute per identity, dropping unverified capacity to an operational nadir. However, adversaries using distilled surrogate models can solve challenges with far less compute.
